name: The Vestige
description: A narrow corridor of pre-Meridian architecture preserved — some say imprisoned — within the megacity's northward expansion, the Vestige is a six-block stretch of late 20th and early 22nd century residential and commercial buildings that a coalition of preservation interests, academic institutions, and wealthy nostalgia investors have maintained in a state of deliberate historical stasis. The buildings have been reinforced, weatherproofed, and in some cases entirely reconstructed from archival photographs, but they are kept deliberately free of visible modern infrastructure. Power and data lines run beneath the streets. Climate control is hidden inside original-looking facade elements. The effect is unsettling — a pocket of another era surrounded on all sides by Meridian's towers.

atmosphere.feel: Profoundly artificial in its authenticity — a place where the past has been taxidermied rather than preserved, and the people who live and work here exist in a performance of history that benefits interests they may not fully understand.

demographics: A small permanent resident population of academics, preservation staff, and the extremely wealthy who pay extraordinary sums for 'authentic' addresses. A much larger daily population of tourism workers, students from the attached university annex, and researchers. The buildings' actual heritage community — descendants of the neighborhoods that existed here — are largely absent, priced and curated out.
economy: Heritage tourism, academic research grants, luxury residential leasing at rates that exclude essentially everyone, corporate event hosting in 'authentic historical settings,' and a significant underground economy among preservation staff who supplement their incomes by facilitating after-hours access for clients who want the Vestige without the curated experience.
power_structure: The Meridian Heritage Conservancy, a nominally nonprofit organization controlled in practice by a board of five investment entities, holds total administrative control. Meridian city government defers entirely to Conservancy decisions within the perimeter. Informal power rests with long-tenured preservation staff who know where every camera blind spot and access tunnel is located.

notable_locations.name: The Alderman's Block
notable_locations.description: The most intact and heavily curated section of the Vestige, a full city block maintained to represent a specific month in 2119. Every surface, every storefront, every parked vehicle is period-accurate. It is rented exclusively for corporate immersive experience events and costs more per night than most Meridian residents earn in a year.

notable_locations.name: Linden Annex
notable_locations.description: The Meridian University historical research outpost embedded in the Vestige, occupying a converted pre-Meridian library building. Publicly a research facility, it maintains the only physical archive of pre-Meridian municipal records in the corridor — and controls access to them with quiet ferocity.

notable_locations.name: The Gap
notable_locations.description: An irregular no-man's-land at the Vestige's southern edge where the preservation boundary meets an unfinished Meridian development project that stalled in litigation. Neither maintained nor demolished, this stretch of partially constructed modern buildings interspersed with unpreserved original structures is the only place in the Vestige where both eras exist simultaneously and honestly.
